before: Every command commit is its own local undo entry, and the shared undo manager groups local journals only by its capture window.
after: A command can name a history group; consecutive commits in one group are one local undo entry, and the shared undo manager starts a new item at each group boundary and keeps one item across a group however long it lasts.
reason: The group token is process-local identity kept beside the journal, never on it, so operations, snapshots, shared state, and protocol messages are unchanged. A replica without the change interoperates because grouping only shapes each replica's own undo stack.
